lead.text: For every consequential thing you consider — a job, a decision, a relationship, a purchase, a public position — run four questions.
Not: is it comforting. Not: is it convenient. Is it true? What is the evidence? What would prove it wrong?
First-order and second-order. In a week, in a year, in a decade. For me and for the people it affects.
Every action votes for a version of you. Which version does this vote for? Is that the version you can respect?
Not in the abstract. To you, in this specific life, given what you have already chosen to care about. If not, why is it in your calendar?

blocks.text: *• What kind of person do I want to become?*
*• What do I want my life to stand for?*

These are not questions you answer once. They are questions you sit with, revisit, and let mature. Your answers at 25 should not be your answers at 55. What should not change is the discipline of asking them.
*“Four questions. Sit with them. Come back to them. They are the exam that never ends.”*
